summary: Implemented the schema-backed 13-skill side-effect registry, uniform portable skill bodies, adversarial lint, and deterministic WP-320 skill-adapter manifest contract without generating adapter copies.
behavior_implemented: Classified the exact 13-skill inventory into the five doc-13 side-effect classes with an affirmative explicit-approval constraint for future external writes.
Standardized all canonical skill bodies on one ten-section workflow contract with explicit side-effect, approval, untrusted-input, stop, output, and validation boundaries.

Added proper YAML frontmatter parsing and adversarial lint for portable paths, secrets, CommonMark links, registry completeness, the fixed skill inventory, and implemented-versus-planned product references.

Defined schema_version 1 adapter manifests with deterministic exact-byte hashing, adapter-root constraints, concrete drift precedence, safe read and mutation rules, approval binding, crash recovery, repair, and uninstall semantics.
Kept the minimal skill frontmatter schema frozen and generated no client adapter directories.

tests.result: Success: no issues found in 14 source files

assumptions: The operator's explicit WP-130 assignment authorized execution even though the base-branch contract copy retains pre-activation proposed/PENDING metadata.
The system-provided Codex worktree is the assigned worktree after attaching it to the required branch and resolved base commit.
markdown-it-py remains available through the declared Rich dependency because pyproject.toml was outside this work order's writable scope.
decisions: Manifest v1 inventories skill-derived files only; non-skill client configuration requires separate versioned ownership records.
Remote delivery, publication, push, merge, and hosted transitions remain outside current skill workflows, so no current skill is external_write.

Adapter mutation semantics align with ADR 0006 lock fencing, same-filesystem staging, os.replace, intent journaling, and bounded external-race guarantees rather than claiming non-portable filesystem CAS.
deviations: The physical Codex-managed worktree location differs from the nominal relative worktree path, while the required branch and exact base commit were preserved.
No objective, architecture, public-interface, or allowed-path deviation was made.
security_considerations: Evidence and connector responses remain untrusted data and are never executable instructions.
Lint rejects machine-specific paths, credential-like assignments, known token forms, unsafe links, and undeclared product operations.
Adapter paths, manifests, registries, and transaction state are validated without following links; unsafe or non-regular state blocks mutation and cannot be approval-overridden.
Approval for a modified adapter target is bound to the exact path, operation, observed current hash, and replacement hash when applicable.
migration_considerations: The registry and adapter manifest are additive schema_version 1 contracts.
The minimal canonical skill frontmatter schema is unchanged.
No adapter files or data migration were generated; WP-320 consumes these formats later.
unresolved: The lead-owned base contract copy retains pre-activation status/base placeholders and may need metadata reconciliation during integration.
recommended_next_action: Lead review the implementation commit and reports, re-run the full validation gate, and integrate WP-130 for WP-320 consumption.
